question: How does the sugar mix of a hydrolysate change the monomer composition of the polymer?

claims.text: Per the cited review's framing, even-carbon volatile fatty acid feeds tend to yield 3HB monomer, while odd-carbon feeds yield 3HV and longer-chain monomers; this was shown with simple substrates such as single VFAs or VFA mixtures, not with sugar hydrolysates.

passages.quote: Generally, even-carbon VFAs tend to generate 3-hydroxybutyrate (3HB) monomer, whereas odd-carbon VFAs yield 3-hydroxyvalerate (3HV) and other longer-chain monomers, which has been clearly evidenced by studies employing simple substrates, such as sole VFA or a VFAs mixture.

claims.text: In Halogeometricum borinquense strain E3, the 3HV fraction of the P(3HB-co-3HV) copolymer was lower when grown on sugarcane bagasse hydrolysate than on glucose medium, which the authors attribute possibly to hydrolysate byproducts inhibiting propionyl-CoA supply.

passages.quote: The drastic reduction in 3HV units from 21.47% (glucose) to 13.29% (SCB) could be due to the inhibition of propionyl-coenzyme A synthesis, an important precursor of 3HV monomer by various byproducts of the SCB hydrolysate.

claims.text: No record in the corpus measures PHA monomer composition across a controlled series of glucose-to-xylose (or other sugar-mix) ratios in a hydrolysate, so the direct effect of the sugar mix on monomer fractions in a single pure-culture system is not established here.

gaps: A controlled experiment varying the glucose:xylose (or hexose:pentose) ratio of a hydrolysate with monomer composition (mol%) measured at each ratio, in one strain under fixed conditions.
Monomer composition data for PHB-producing pure cultures (for example Cupriavidus necator or Burkholderia sacchari) grown on xylose versus glucose mixtures, with mol% 3HV reported.
Direct evidence on which hydrolysate inhibitors or co-products change propionyl-CoA or acyl-CoA precursor supply; the Halogeometricum explanation is the authors' hypothesis, not a measured mechanism.
Most cited monomer-composition values come from unverified curation notes or mixed-culture VFA studies; no verified record links a hydrolysate sugar mix to monomer fractions.
Whether the mixed-culture VFA-to-monomer trend applies to sugar-derived precursors, which the corpus does not test.

passages.heading: 3. Results and Discussion › 3.6. Polymer Characterization › 3.6.5. 1H-NMR Analysis
passages.text: Interestingly, copolymer P(3HB-co-3HV)] containing a higher amount of 3HV (21.47% 3HV) was synthesized by the same E3 strain in NSM media with glucose as the substrate. The drastic reduction in 3HV units from 21.47% (glucose) to 13.29% (SCB) could be due to the inhibition of propionyl-coenzyme A synthesis, an important precursor of 3HV monomer by various byproducts of the SCB hydrolysate. PHA accumulation by extremely halophilic archaea and moderately halophilic and/or halotolerant bacteria, inhabiting hypersaline and marine regions of countries such as China, Turkey, Bolivia, Vietnam, India, etc., has been documented.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Generally, even-carbon VFAs tend to generate 3-hydroxybutyrate (3HB) monomer, whereas odd-carbon VFAs yield 3-hydroxyvalerate (3HV) and other longer-chain monomers, which has been clearly evidenced by studies employing simple substrates, such as sole VFA or a VFAs mixture. The monomer composition of PHA subsequently determines the thermal and mechanical properties of the polymer, including its elasticity, crystallinity and rigidness. The homopolymer poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) is a very crystalline and stiff material with a high melting point, which hinders its processing and commercial applications. To improve the properties of pure PHB, incorporating 3HV and other longer-chain monomers will lead to ameliorative attributes, such as a decreased melting point and increased ductility.
